newsitem.title: USA: Gilead says to file NDA for herpes gel.
newsitem.headline: Gilead says to file NDA for herpes gel.

text.p: Gilead Sciences Inc said on Wednesday that it expected to file, in the first quarter of 1997, a New Drug Application (NDA) for the use of its topical Forvade (cidofovir gel) product in the treatment of the Herpes Simplex virus in patients with AIDS.

Speaking at a Robertson Stephens & Co-sponsored medical conference in New York, the company's Senior Vice President of Product Development, Howard Jaffe, said that clinical studies had shown the product to be effective in treating herpes that had not responded to approved therapies.

Cidofovir gel is one of a new class of antiviral compounds known as nucleotide analogues. They are said to inhibit viral replication through less frequent dosage than currently available viral medication.

Separately, Vice President Linda Fitzpatrick told Reuters in a telephone conversation that Gilead was in the process of expanding its sales force by about 25 percent to promote its lead drug Vistide -- used for treating an eye condition in AIDS patients that can lead to blindness -- as well as Hoffman-La Roche Inc's Roferon-A drug, used in the treatment of hepatitis C.
Gilead entered into a collaboration with Hoffman-La Roche in September to co-promote Roferon in the United States, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
Hoffman La-Roche, a unit of Roche Holding Ltd, announced last month that it had received the marketing clearance.
